clue.text: Hand over, say, a tray after hour dipped in lead

indicators.note: something dipped in is plunged inside, so the hour-and-tray run sits within the metal's symbol

parts.note: PB is the chemical symbol for the metal lead (Latin plumbum)

indicators.note: the tray comes after the hour, so it follows it in the run

parts.note: a salver is a flat serving tray

explanation.surface: Someone passes a tray to another person after an hour spent with it plunged in molten metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb but is the metal, and 'dipped in' makes it the container. 'say' marks the definition as an example: 'hand over' is one such verb-plus-particle expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb plus particle with its own meaning, such as hand over, is a grammatical example of this category.

clue.text: Fop gets to drop by on bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the visit comes first

parts.note: to pop in is to drop by for a casual visit
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A dandy turns up at a friend's house with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a vain, showily dressed man, originally meaning a parrot.

clue.text: It's an instrument — that's official

definitions.meaning: a woodwind instrument played by blowing into the end
a judicial officer, or someone who keeps official records

explanation.surface: A cheerful statement that something is officially a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a simple fipple flute and a part-time judge or keeper of records.

clue.text: Girl owns up about artist

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the artist
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: owns means has
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A girl confesses something concerning a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the word for owns from the bottom, and 'about' wraps that turned word round the artist, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so a straightforward example of a girl.

definitions.meaning: 25 down means drunk, and a very drunk person is too unsteady to stand
14 down is a pink wriggling creature that has no limbs at all

explanation.surface: Cross-references asking whether one entry describes another.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions point at other entries: 25 down (drunk) and 14 down, a creature without limbs; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely drunk, and also literally lacking limbs, like a worm.

clue.text: Design of castile adaptable

indicators.note: a design is an arrangement, so the letters of the soap name are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A soap bar's shape can be changed to suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Castile is a kind of olive-oil soap as well as a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy and flexible can adjust to circumstances, the figurative sense of springy.

clue.text: Accommodation that's little improved, housing daughter, is shown up

indicators.note: housing means the better word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: improved means better

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means read from the bottom, so the little word runs backwards

explanation.surface: A small flat has been upgraded, takes in a daughter, and is put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' belongs to the definition, since a bedsit is small. 'shown up' turns the little word upside down in this down clue; 'housing' puts the daughter and it inside the word for improved.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a one-room flat where the occupant sleeps and lives in the same space.

clue.text: Watch the drink during conversation

indicators.note: in conversation words are spoken, so we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the drink while you are talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch something is to look at it, a direct synonym for observing.

clue.text: Partner puts first of pants in to soak

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the soaking word

parts.note: to souse is to soak or drench

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A husband or wife leaves some trousers to steep in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is one's partner in marriage.

clue.text: Box you upended, opening for seamstress

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means turned on end, so the run is read backwards

parts.note: the box and the tele are both informal words for television
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A punch thrown at someone turned upside down creates a chance for a dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' reverses TELE + YE as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reinforced hole in fabric for a lace or cord to pass through, which a sewer makes.

clue.text: Horse given last of syrup (maple)

indicators.note: last of means take the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: Acer is the botanical name for the maple genus

explanation.surface: A horse is given a treat of maple syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred or trained to run at a lateral gait in harness racing.

clue.text: Relative amount, one claimed, impressive

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: claimed means taken in, so the amount holds the numeral inside

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A relative receives a dose of something and claims it is impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and showy in style, which comes across as imposing or impressive.

clue.text: In home, value's heading to the bottom — that's the point

indicators.note: in means the moved word sits inside the home word

parts.note: a nest is a home

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, goes to the bottom, the end of the word

parts.note: value is worth; the apostrophe s just joins it to its action

explanation.surface: House prices are slumping, and that is the whole idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'value's heading to the bottom' reads like falling house prices, but it moves the first letter of the word for value to its end before 'In' sets it inside the home.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point between the two named directions, so one of the points of the compass.

clue.text: One's a woman? It's debatable!

parts.note: one is I, and the apostrophe s adds S
Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is female and is told the point is open to argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under dispute is a topic that is open to debate.

clue.text: Like Peter Pan found in stage lessons

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An actor playing Peter Pan picked up some acting tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy who never grows up never gets any older, so stays forever young.

clue.text: Pink thing getting warmer, hot after a thrashing

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks things about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A pink object grows warmer and then hot after being beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of a common soil invertebrate by its colour.

clue.text: Sound place to mention

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a site is a place

explanation.surface: A good location to bring up a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote or refer to something is to mention it.

clue.text: Old chancellor and Jewish teacher deprived of a British vegetable

parts.note: Helmut Kohl was chancellor of Germany

indicators.note: deprived of means a letter is taken away

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: A former chancellor and a rabbi lose a British vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip-like cabbage variety whose swollen stem is eaten.

clue.text: State of which East End boy has knowledge

parts.note: Del Boy is the East London market trader in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses
to be aware is to have knowledge of something

explanation.surface: A US state that a Cockney lad knows about.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class district of London; Del Boy is its best-known television son.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of the United States to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Stuff remains at the vineyard to be knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: marc is the residue of skins and pips left after grapes are pressed

explanation.surface: Leftovers at a winery are drunk down.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff is to pack something full, as one does when filling a space tightly.

clue.text: Face trap, heading for gaol for criminal act

parts.note: mug is slang for face
a gin is a snare or trap

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A trap set for someone's face, then they head to prison for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A street robbery with violence or threats, a criminal act.

clue.text: Doctor's cutting instrument beginning to extract bodily substance

indicators.note: the doctor is cutting into the instrument, so it sits inside

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; the apostrophe s just joins it

indicators.note: beginning means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A surgeon's scalpel starts to extract some bodily fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting instrument' reads as a scalpel, but 'cutting' is the container indicator and the instrument is a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical messenger secreted by glands into the blood, a substance the body produces.

clue.text: Game where drawing may lead to suspension?

definitions.text: Game where drawing may lead to suspension?

parts.words: Game where drawing may lead to suspension?
parts.note: in this pencil game a figure on a gallows is drawn bit by bit for each wrong guess

explanation.surface: A sport where a tie may get a player banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests a drawn match and 'suspension' a ban; in fact a stick figure is sketched hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A word-guessing game in which wrong letters build a picture of a figure on a gallows.

clue.text: Dahl novel among books, stale

indicators.note: among means the scrambled name sits inside the books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the name are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A Roald Dahl novel on the shelves has gone out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something already familiar and unoriginal is dull and stale.

clue.text: Senior nurse takes temperature, feeding a month later

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the letter is put inside the month

parts.note: Mar is short for March
on means later, as in from then on

explanation.surface: A head nurse takes a patient's temperature and puts a feeding off a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior nursing officer in a hospital or a school's resident nurse.

clue.text: Lead short, short, 60% off lead

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sixty percent off a five-letter word removes three letters, keeping just its first two

explanation.surface: A clipped instruction about a lead cut by more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap for walking a dog is called a lead in Britain.

clue.text: Again I let out the privates

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once again a soldier gives leave to the privates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' suggests army ranks, but it is the slang for private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The external sexual organs, euphemistically called one's privates.

clue.text: Drunk in snug

definitions.meaning: intoxicated, informally said of someone who has had too much
fitting closely without room to spare

explanation.surface: A man is drunk in a cosy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both intoxicated and closely fitting.

clue.text: Instrument's drone inspiring A minor fantasia

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the hum takes the scrambled letters inside

parts.note: a drone is a low hum

indicators.note: a fantasia is a free-form composition, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A keyboard's drone sets off a fantasia in A minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantasia' rearranges A MINOR, and 'inspiring' (breathing in) makes the drone take those letters between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reed organ with a keyboard, pumped by pedals.

clue.text: Part through an African country

indicators.note: a part is a piece of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Travelling partly through a country in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'country'; 'African' supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African nation, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Figure after tax returns

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: net pay is pay after tax

explanation.surface: A sum calculated after one files tax returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax returns' reads as forms; 'returns' is the reversal indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A number, the figure that comes after nine.

clue.text: French defence a long time in manoeuvres

indicators.note: military manoeuvres move troops about, so the letters are moved into new places

explanation.surface: French forces spent ages on exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of fortifications France built along its eastern border before the Second World War.
